百姓Hyakushō

How to hold a village together

Four peasants, one valley, four years. Nothing happens until you end the turn, so there is no hurry — only consequences.

  1. Your first year is nearly free. Newly opened land is taxed lightly, so the first levy asks only 18 koku. Use the year to learn the valley. The asking then climbs: 55, then 100, then 155.
  2. Standing, not strikes. Falling short costs the castle's regard in proportion to how far short you fall — a few koku is a note in a ledger, half the demand is a mark against the village. Run it to nothing and the village is broken up. Tap the levy chip to read the ledger.
  3. There is more than one way to pay. Traders come up the valley with a single offer — timber for rice, rice for stone, take it or leave it. A village that cuts bamboo or traps fish can buy its way to the levy without a paddy in sight.
  4. The ground decides the harvest. Paddies ripen half again as fast on reed marsh, slowly on dry moor. Bamboo pays less than pine but grows back inside the year. Read the valley before you plan it.
  5. Build shelter before winter. A Minka sleeps two; villagers without a bed lose heart. A Hearth Fire keeps anyone within five tiles alive through the cold. A Kura raises how much you can store — everything over the cap rots.
  6. You give orders, not commands. Choose a work order or a building, then drag across the map. Villagers pick up the nearest job they are willing to do; the toggles under each name in Village decide what that is.
  7. Bandits come from year two. Villagers fight automatically when one gets close. A Yagura makes them fight harder; an Ishigaki makes bandits waste turns breaking through.
  8. Tap a villager to hear what they are thinking. Their spirit is not a mood dial — it is a list of reasons, each one named and counted. Fix the reasons and the number follows. Tap their name to call them something of your own.

Moving the map: drag with no tool chosen to pan, pinch or scroll to zoom, tap a tile to inspect it, tap a villager to select them. While a tool is chosen, dragging paints instead — tap the chip at the bottom of the map to put it down.

Keyboard: Space end turn · B build menu · C/M/F work orders · X cancel tool · Esc put the tool down · H this page
